claims.text: Mechanical alloying of W–Cu powders before SPS will significantly reduce voids relative to vapor-coated W-powder sintering.
Mechanical alloying of W–Cu powders before SPS will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding relative to vapor-coated W-powder sintering.
Mechanical alloying activates the surfaces of W and Cu powders.
Mechanical alloying cleans W and Cu particle surfaces.
Mechanical alloying partially deforms W and Cu particle surfaces.
Mechanical alloying promotes atomic-level mixing of W and Cu.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS produces enhanced W–Cu interfacial contact and greater boundary homogeneity.
Enhanced W–Cu interfacial contact and homogeneity reduce porosity in the final composite.
Enhanced W–Cu interfacial contact and homogeneity reduce phase separation in the final composite.
Pressure and rapid heating during SPS densify mechanically alloyed W–Cu particles more effectively.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS leads to near-perfect W–Cu interfacial contact.
The proposed process produces a uniform microstructure that suppresses void formation.
The proposed W–Cu composite will have a significantly lower void fraction than a composite made from vapor-coated W powders sintered under similar conditions.
The proposed W–Cu composite will have improved thermal conductivity relative to the vapor-coated-powder baseline.
The proposed W–Cu composite will preserve mechanical durability relative to the vapor-coated-powder baseline.
Vapor-coated W powders can be sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between W and Cu.
The vapor-coated W-powder baseline has inherent limitations from possible residual defects.
Excessive milling can cause contamination or amorphization.
Extreme deviations in milling or SPS parameters could negate the proposed benefits.
Scaling mechanical alloying while maintaining process consistency may introduce variability.

contradictions.description: The requested SPS temperature is described as both below the boiling point of Cu and near the melting point of W; given the widely separated temperatures stated in the query, these boundaries are difficult to satisfy simultaneously and are not operationally defined.

The experiment says the groups differ only by the mechanical-alloying step, but the named baseline uses vapor-coated W powder while the proposed feedstock is mechanically alloyed. It is unclear whether vapor coating is retained in the intervention group, so coating status may also differ.
